name: Synchrovet
description: Synchrovet is a neurochemical calibration agent that temporarily optimizes the electrochemical environment at BCI neural interfaces, improving signal clarity, reducing latency artifacts, and smoothing out the misfires that cause 'neural static' — the disorienting sensory noise that affects poorly calibrated or aging BCI hardware. It is taken before high-precision BCI work or after interface hardware updates.
effects: suppresses neural static and interface artifacts
improves BCI precision and response fidelity
smooths sensory translation from digital inputs
side_effects: hyperawareness of digital inputs during peak effect
post-dose sensory dulling as brain recalibrates
can cause interface feedback loops in damaged hardware
cultural_context: Synchrovet occupies a gray zone between medical necessity and enhancement. Surgeons, pilots, precision operators, and competitive gamers use it professionally. The mild euphoria and the sensation of perfect digital-organic alignment make it recreationally appealing — the addiction risk comes from people chasing that feeling of frictionless clarity. On the street it's called 'the tune' because users describe it as being in perfect pitch with their hardware.
story_hooks: A surgeon is addicted to Synchrovet and their hands are only steady when dosed — their patients don't know
A black market Synchrovet analog is causing permanent BCI calibration drift — users who take it enough times find their interface never feels right again without it
A character discovers that Synchrovet's calibration effect also makes BCI users temporarily more susceptible to specific neural-frequency intrusion signals
